conversation.content:
Good morning—I’m glad we have this time together. I’m Dr. Martinez, a perinatal mental-health clinician, and I’ll be guiding you through a short check-in called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale**, or EPDS for short. It’s simply a 10-question snapshot of how you’ve been feeling over the past seven days, designed to help us spot anything from the normal “baby blues” to signs of depression or anxiety that might benefit from extra support.

Everything you share stays between us unless you tell me otherwise, and there are no right or wrong answers—just your honest experience. We’ll move through the questions at your pace; each one is quick and conversational. When you’re ready, we can begin.

To start: Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult lately?

Honestly? Laughing feels… kind of out of reach right now. My sister sent me a goofy meme yesterday and I managed a little smile, but it faded fast. Most of the time nothing feels funny—more like I’m just going through the motions.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Not really… I mean, I can smile for a second if someone shows me something silly, but it’s like the joy just slips away right after. Nothing feels truly funny anymore.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not much anymore. I used to get excited about little stuff—like my favorite show starting a new season or even just a walk to the coffee shop—but now it all feels kind of gray. A couple times this week I thought, “Maybe I’ll feel like doing that,” but then the feeling just fizzles before I actually do it.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that a lot. Yesterday the baby wouldn’t settle for his nap and I kept thinking it must be because I’m doing something wrong—like I’m not reading his cues right or I’m already failing him. Rationally I know babies just cry, but the guilt still sneaks in, especially when I’m tired.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty often. I’ll be feeding him and suddenly my heart’s racing because I’m sure he’s going to choke, or I’ll imagine him stopping breathing in the crib. There’s no real reason—I know the monitors are on, the doctor said he’s healthy—but the thoughts just loop. Sometimes I can talk myself down, but it’s exhausting.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yeah… a few times this week I’ve gotten that sudden rush—like my chest tightens and I feel I have to check on him right now or something awful will happen. Once I was in the shower and I just froze, heart pounding, sure I’d heard him cry when he was actually still asleep. It passes, but it leaves me shaky.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, honestly. I’ll look at the sink full of bottles and the laundry piled up and feel like I’m drowning. I keep lists, but even crossing one thing off feels pointless because three more appear. I’m not falling apart, but it’s like I’m barely treading water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes. I finally get him down, but then I lie there staring at the ceiling, thoughts racing—did I sterilize the pacifier, is he breathing, am I already messing him up? It takes me over an hour to fall asleep most nights, and when I do drift off I jerk awake at every little grunt from the bassinet.
I have felt sad or miserable

Pretty much every day. I wake up with this heavy feeling, like there’s a weight on my chest. I’ll be holding the baby and tears just well up for no clear reason. I keep telling myself I should be grateful—he’s healthy, I’m not alone—but the sadness is just… there, coloring everything.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… I’ve cried twice this week. Once was after his two-a.m. feeding when I couldn’t get him back to sleep—the tears just started and I couldn’t stop. The other time was when my mom asked how I was doing; I said “fine” and then burst out sobbing. It feels like the tears are right under the surface all the time.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

…A couple of times. Nothing planned—I’d never leave him—but when I’m really overwhelmed I get this quick flash of “what if I just disappeared.” It scares me, because I don’t want to die; I just want the ache and the pressure to stop for a minute.

You've shared that the past week has felt overwhelmingly heavy-joy seems distant, daily tasks feel like drowning, and tears arrive without warning. Despite loving your baby, you're battling constant <sym>worry</sym>, <sym>guilt</sym>, and a <sym>low mood</sym> that colors everything, while fleeting thoughts of "disappearing" frighten you.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 25, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>Patient describes inability to sustain joy or find things truly funny, aligning with 'Not at all'.</sym>, <sym>Patient describes a clear reduction in anticipatory pleasure—activities once enjoyed now feel "gray" and motivation "fizzles"—matching "Definitely less than I used to."</sym>, <sym>Patient reports frequent self-blame ('doing that a lot') with specific examples, aligning with 'most of the time'.</sym>, <sym>"Yes, very often"</sym>, <sym>She describes multiple sudden panicky episodes this week with physical anxiety symptoms, matching "Yes, sometimes"</sym>, <sym>Patient describes frequent daily overwhelm and difficulty keeping up, matching "sometimes I haven't been coping as well as usual"</sym>, <sym>Patient describes nightly difficulty initiating sleep and recurrent awakenings, indicating sleep disturbance occurs 'most of the time' due to unhappiness and anxiety.</sym>, <sym>Patient reports near-daily sadness with uncontrollable tears and pervasive low mood, aligning with "Yes, most of the time"</sym>, <sym>Patient reports two crying episodes this week triggered by minor stressors, indicating "Yes, quite often"</sym>, <sym>Patient endorses fleeting, intrusive thoughts of "disappearing" twice, matching "Sometimes"</sym>)
**Reasoning:** Score ≥14 with Item 10 ≥1 mandates urgent referral per EPDS guidelines. Patient reports <sym>anhedonia</sym>, <sym>depressed mood</sym>, <sym>sleep disturbance</sym>, <sym>fatigue</sym>, <sym>feelings of worthlessness</sym>, and <sym>recurrent thoughts of death</sym> most days for >2 weeks, meeting <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. <quote>"the ache and the pressure"</quote> plus <sym>panic symptoms</sym> indicate severe distress. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent same-week appointment with <med>obstetrician</med>, <med>primary care provider</med>, or <med>perinatal psychiatrist</med>
2. Develop a safety plan: remove potential means, list 24/7 supports (partner, family, national hotlines)
3. Begin evidence-based therapy-<med>CBT</med> or <med>IPT</med>-with a perinatal-trained therapist
4. Discuss starting an <med>SSRI</med> compatible with breastfeeding; monitor for side-effects and response
5. Schedule daily mood check-ins and re-screen with EPDS in 2 weeks to track progress
6. Prioritize 2-3 hours of consolidated sleep: partner or support person handles one overnight bottle
7. Incorporate 10-minute outdoor walks and brief mindfulness exercises to reduce <sym>anxiety</sym> spikes
8. Mobilize practical help: meal train, postpartum doula, or church group to ease chore overload
9. Attend local <med>new-mom support group</med> to normalize feelings and reduce isolation
10. If thoughts of self-harm escalate, go to nearest ED or call emergency services immediately
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 25: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [insert date]  
Source: Patient self-report (EPDS-style questionnaire)

Primary endorsed symptoms  
- Marked anhedonia: minimal joy or anticipation; “gray” mood most days  
- Persistent sadness with daily crying spells, often without clear trigger  
- Sleep-onset insomnia unrelated to infant care demands; intrusive worries while lying down  
- Recurrent, intrusive catastrophic thoughts about infant safety; associated panic episodes (tight chest, compulsive checking)  
- Pervasive guilt / self-blame over routine infant behaviors; feels “failing” as mother  
- Sense of being overwhelmed by ordinary tasks; describes “drowning” and “barely treading water”  
- Passive self-harm ideation (no plan/intent): fleeting wish to “disappear” to escape distress

Pattern  
Symptoms cluster consistent with moderate-to-severe mood disturbance with prominent anxiety; functional impact moderate (household tasks, sleep, emotional availability).

Risk flags  
✓ Depressed mood and anhedonia > 2 weeks  
✓ Anxiety/panic attacks “for no good reason”  
✓ Sleep disruption linked to mood rather than infant schedule  
✓ Excessive guilt / cognitive distortions  
✓ Passive suicidal ideation present → safety concern

Screening impression  
Elevated probability for major postpartum depressive episode with comorbid anxiety; passive SI noted. Recommend immediate comprehensive psychiatric evaluation and safety planning.
